**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A small white paper plate. Judged against almond size (about 2.3 cm long each), it is about 17 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 8.5² ≈ 227 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Whole almonds, about 26 visible. No oil or seasoning is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The almond cluster covers about 22% of the plate, roughly 50 cm². The rest of the plate is empty, so the total covered share is about 22%.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** 50 cm² × 0.8 cm (single layer of almonds) ≈ 40 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** 40 ml × 0.7 g/ml (whole nuts with gaps) ≈ 28 g. As a cross-check, about 26 almonds × 1.2 g each ≈ 31 g. I'll use about 30 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Almonds have about 579 kcal per 100 g, so 30 g × 5.79 ≈ 174 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Roughly 26 almonds is about one standard 1 oz (28 g) serving, which is about 160–175 kcal. The estimate is plausible.
